keyFacts: The USWNT played Spain at Subaru Park in Chester, Pennsylvania, for their second international friendly of the fall.

body: CHESTER, PA. — The U.S. women hope to exact revenge on the world's top-ranked side as they meet defending World Cup champions Spain for the second of two international friendlies this fall.

The USWNT was beaten 2-0 in their first meeting in the nation's capital on Saturday, downed by two early goals from Spain, which then weathered the rest of the match effectively. Emma Hayes tried to engineer a comeback, with the U.S. outshooting Spain 13-6 and logging significantly more goal-mouth action in general, but the hosts failed to breach the net in the end.

Now, looking to prove the top spot in FIFA's rankings belong to them, the second-ranked United States give it another go on home soil, aiming to prove the first meeting was a fluke and they remain the favorites to win next summer's Women's World Cup.

As rumors will continue to surround the Yankees ahead of the offseason, one MLB insider discusses the possibility of the team trading Luis Garcia Jr., who was acquired last year by New York from the Washington Nationals.

Last season, Garcia produced on an impressive level, recording a cumulative .277 batting average with 30 home runs and 92 RBIs, whereas in the 43 games played with the Yankees, he had a .264 average, seven home runs and 16 RBIs. Joel Sherman spoke on “Pinstripe Post,” via The New York Post, and pontificated Garcia being a trade chip since he will be a free agent in 2027 , and threw out a team that could use him.

“He’s a free agent after the 2027 season; we are probably going to get, if not a salary cap, some tougher penalties for the upper end of payrolls. And I can’t imagine the Yankees would probably figure they’re going to have to pay Ben Rice at some point, re-signing another like player long term for big money. articles.headline: Is Mini DisplayPort becoming obsolete?
keyFacts: Apple and PC makers phased out Mini DisplayPort after Thunderbolt 3 switched to the USB-C connector.
USB-C replaced Mini DisplayPort because it handles video, audio, and high-speed data through a single reversible connector.
Full-size DisplayPort remains standard for high-end monitors, while upcoming HDMI 2.2 devices may soon offer competitive bandwidth.
body: Is Mini DisplayPort becoming obsolete?
How Thunderbolt and USB-C replaced the need for a dedicated video port.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

For a while, Mini DisplayPort was one of the main options for video output on smaller devices. Apple announced it in 2008 to replace interfaces like VGA and DVI with a single, slimmer connector. While it was seen on most Mac models for several years, it's since become difficult to find computers with Mini DisplayPort — even Apple has removed the port from Macs.

But does that mean it's obsolete? Not exactly, although you won't see it as often as you used to. The DisplayPort standard remains popular, especially among workstations and gaming monitors, so it's not as if the technology itself has become obsolete. But we now have another small port that's favored.
Why Mini DisplayPort faded out

Mini DisplayPort is called "mini" for a reason. The full-size version (simply called DisplayPort) supports the same core specifications, but with a larger connector. Apple always opted for the tiny version because it fits better on smaller computers like MacBooks and the Mac mini.

It doesn't matter whether you use DisplayPort (DP) or Mini DisplayPort — both can transmit video and audio through a single cable. Compared to older connectors like DVI and VGA, one of the main advantages of DisplayPort is that it offers much higher bandwidth. Depending on the generation, DP can handle resolutions up to 8K and beyond, at high frame rates (144+Hz) depending on the resolution. Meanwhile, older connectors struggle with anything above 1080p.

When the Thunderbolt standard emerged, its first two iterations used the Mini DisplayPort connector. While a standard Mini DP port only carries video and audio, Thunderbolt also supports high-speed data transfers. That meant the same connector could be used for video, audio and data — perfect for accessories like Apple's Cinema Display.

In late 2015 and 2016, the Thunderbolt 3 standard arrived and switched to the USB-C connector. Apple and other PC manufacturers quickly moved to USB-C or HDMI, leaving the Mini DisplayPort connector behind. These days, USB-C has become the standard for nearly everything. Not only can it support high-speed data transfer, but it can also handle video, audio and even the Thunderbolt protocol — all in a single, small reversible connector. Not every USB-C port can handle the same tasks, but you'll see some version of it on almost every device.

To further push Mini DisplayPort down, USB-C also supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode, meaning a compatible USB-C cable and ports can carry the same DisplayPort signal through the more modern cable. PC makers have no reason to have people buy a Mini DP-to-DP cable when they can simply buy a USB-C-to-DP cable.
Where DisplayPort still makes sense

That doesn't mean DisplayPort is gone. Of course, you may still find older hardware with Mini DisplayPort, like past laptops and graphics cards. If you still have one of these, you can buy a Mini DP-to-DP cable to connect them to a modern monitor. Since the protocol is the same, they'll communicate with each other just fine. New hardware also continues to use full-sized version of DisplayPort. It's still the standard for many high-end monitors and graphics cards.

HDMI has come a long way in recent years and can now transmit video at incredibly high resolutions. Still, DisplayPort remains the gold standard for absurdly high resolutions and refresh rates, such as 4K at 240Hz. For comparison, while HDMI 2.1 offers up to 48 Gbps of bandwidth, DisplayPort 2.1 can reach 80 Gbps. This makes a difference for those looking to get the most out of the hardware they have. HDMI 2.2 offers 96 Gbps bandwidth, which may even the field a bit once compatible devices are widely available.

Of course, when using older hardware, not everything may work as expected. VR headsets, for example, can be picky about their video signal, and they don't always play nice with Mini DisplayPort when you use an adapter. The same goes for the old Apple Cinema Display — Apple makes it clear that it doesn't work through a Thunderbolt adapter. Still, it doesn't hurt to try if you have the right cables on hand.

articles.headline: Russia resorts to desperate World War One defence technique to protect its oil refineries — floating barrage balloons failed to curtail V1s and are unlikely to succeed against UAVs
keyFacts: Russia deployed barrage balloons with radar-adjusted cables to protect oil refineries from Ukrainian drone attacks.
Protecting oil refineries is vital to Russia's economic strength and supports its invasion of Ukraine.
The new defense strategy has not been tested against Ukrainian strikes and may only affect smaller drones.
body: - Russia has updated the concept of barrage balloons to defend oil refineries
- Barrage balloons were first deployed over 100 years ago to defend against air raids
- It is not clear what the measures are defending against, as they only appear suitable for disabling smaller drones

Russia has deployed barrage balloons around its oil refineries to defend against Ukraine drone attacks – but the demonstration using a small drone has raised questions about the effectiveness of the measure.

Protecting oil refineries from drone strikes is key to Russia’s economic strength and supports its efforts in the invasion and occupation of Ukraine. But while the barrage balloons employ intriguing radar-based altitude-adjusting motors to ensure drones are slowed or caught, the deployment seems unsuited to the drones Ukraine would actually send for such a strike.

Sharing the information via Telegram, the Vesti news organization has reported on the deployment of the modern barrage balloons. But the report has a sense of propaganda, rather than portraying a competent military defense strategy.
Oil refinery targets

Russia’s defense of its oil refineries from Ukrainian drone strikes has so far relied on balloon-attached nets, which are designed to create a barrier. The problem with that solution is that drones can just fly over the net.

So, its latest solution is a series of cables, elevated by barrage balloons, and a system of motors that adjusts the height of the balloons and the cables. This is controlled by a system that uses radar information to detect the height of the incoming drone strike. So far so good – it seems like a sound deployment

But is it successful? To date, the strategy hasn’t been tested. Demonstrations, such as the one shared on Telegram, indicate that smaller unmanned aerial vehicles might run into trouble. However, the demo uses a smaller craft, and it isn’t unreasonable to foresee Ukraine mounting its drones’ wings with blades to cut through the cables...
V1s and UAVs

The original deployment of barrage balloons occurred towards the end of the First World War, when Britain and Germany both employed the countermeasure. Their targets were early aircraft engaging in bombing raids, and the use of balloons was successful enough to be repeated by Britain again in the 1940s to defend against V1 rockets.

Launched from Nazi Germany’s territory, the V1s were essentially single-use drones, rockets deployed with enough fuel to reach the target. But in the 1940s, the use of barrage balloons took out around 200 V1s as they descended onto their targets, but were ineffective against high altitude bombers.

The deployment of barrage balloons by Russia in an attempt to defend its oil refineries appears almost ingenious. But a few moments of analysis indicate the unsuitability of the countermeasure for drones and UAVs, leaving us to suspect that this could merely be some elaborate propaganda.

articles.headline: Ilhan Omar’s husband spotted for first time since DHS raid – as Trump questions how couple can afford their ‘lovely place in Washington’
keyFacts: Homeland Security Investigations agents searched the Washington, D.C., home of Representative Ilhan Omar and husband Tim Mynett on Monday.
The raid is reportedly part of an ongoing criminal fraud investigation into Omar's immigration paperwork.
Donald Trump questioned how the couple could afford their home and suggested Omar engaged in fraudulent activities.
body: Tim Mynett, the husband of embattled Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), was spotted Tuesday for the first time since the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) raided their Washington, DC, home – which President Trump suggested the couple shouldn’t be able to afford.

Mynett, staring straight down at the sidewalk, was snapped walking the family dog – a yellow labrador retriever named Teddy – back to the home where Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents executed a search warrant and removed belongings early Monday morning.
The raid is believed to be part of an ongoing criminal fraud investigation into the Somalia-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.

Trump, who has long accused Omar of illegally marrying her brother, took to Truth Social Tuesday to suggest the “Squad” lawmaker may have been involved in “fraudulent activities” — citing the dramatic rise in the congresswoman’s reported net-worth, which she has since dismissed as an accounting discrepancy.

“Why did Ilhan Omar report a Net Worth of up to 30 Million Dollars just a short time ago, and then immediately say, ‘Oh, I made a mistake! It’s really $100,000,’” Trump wrote. “Could it be that her highly paid accountant actually reported the money that was stolen from her fraudulent activities in Minnesota? Would something like that be possible? Do you think the accountant actually gave the right number the first time, 30 Million Dollars, and then she was forced to disavow because she never would have been able to report where that much money came from?
“She must have freaked out when she saw that money!”

Trump also expressed disbelief that Omar and Mynett had the means to live in their Washington house — a four-bedroom, 1,900-square-foot Cape Cod assessed at about $600,000. Property records do not list Omar or Mynett as owners, and the home has been previously listed for rent.

“Where did her house come from, where did her cars come from, and what about her lovely place in Washington, D.C.?” the president said. “I didn’t know that Congressmen and women made that kind of money, but I do know her husband, according to information and belief, makes almost nothing, so it couldn’t have come from him.”

The Post previously reported that Mynett initially valued his venture capital firm, Rose Lake Capital, and defunct California-based wine business, eStCru, at up to $30 million in Omar’s 2024 financial disclosure.

However, in the congresswoman’s 2025 financial disclosure report, Mynett reported no income from his venture capital firm and only $200 to $1,000 in income from the wine business, which shut down in April.
“How many people did she illegally bring into our Country from Somalia?” Trump continued. “America wants answers, and we want them, NOW!”
Omar’s office did not immediately respond to The Post’s request for comment.

articles.headline: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
keyFacts: Science Corporation implanted its PRIMA vision-restoring chip into its first Stargardt disease patient, CEO Max Hodak announced.
The implant enabled the patient to read a word despite Stargardt disease being currently considered incurable, the company said.
Science Corporation plans to test a next-generation implant in human patients within the next year, Hodak said.
body: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said on stage. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.

While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.

Stargardt disease affects the outer retina, causing the gradual death of the eye’s light-sensing cells while potentially sparing the inner retina, the part that passes visual signals onto the brain. It causes a central blind spot that gradually enlarges over time. Approximately 150,000 people worldwide have lost vision due to the disease.

“One of the nice things about this device approach, when I was saying the brain’s a computer, vision is electrical potential, like electrical activity down the optic nerve,” Hodak said. “That’s all vision is to the brain, and so if you can get the optic nerve to signal the the rest of the brain correctly, then you can provide vision to it.”

The company says its first patient with Stargardt disease received the PRIMA implant in May as part of its ongoing trial at the Sydney Eye Hospital in Australia. During the patient’s first rehabilitation session, he saw a letter, and during the second, he was able to read a word.

To use the device, patients undergo an hour-long procedure that plants a small chip in the back of their eye, where the photoreceptors have degenerated. Then they wear camera-equipped glasses that transmit a view of the world to the chip. The implant essentially works like artificial photoreceptors.

“The device that this patient has is a two millimeter by two millimeter implant placed under the in the back of the eye, and so it’s like looking through a straw,” Hodak said. “It is not a big field of view color vision. It’s a patch in their central vision where . . .it’s black and white, but it is sharp. It’s high-contrast sharp, and so they can see a couple letters at a time. The next step is to make the field of view bigger. So to make a bigger implant, you have to deal with the curvature of the eye, and we need to make the electrodes smaller so that we get closer to native levels of detail.”

He continued, “I think we have a clear path. There’s a there’s a next ‘next generation’ that’s being worked on that’ll be in humans in the next year, and over the next five years, I think we’ll be able to get pretty close to native acuity.”

When Hodak founded Science Corporation in 2021 after leaving Neuralink, the company outlined plans to develop advanced neural engineering and brain-computer interface technology. But first, the company wants to prove its methods work and develop a sustainable business, which is why it’s working to restore vision with the visually impaired.

As for Science Corporation’s brain-computer interface technology, it has previously said that its sensor will be implanted inside the skull and rest on top of the brain, unlike a Neuralink device, which is inserted directly into brain tissue.
The company has said it believes the device could help address neurological conditions, such as possibly monitoring neurological activity in patients with brain tumors.

“In the near term, we’re going to be applying our first clinical indication, which hasn’t been announced publicly, is a neurodegenerative disease that everybody’s heard of,” Hodak said. “We’re also looking at stroke. For example, if you’ve lost part of your brain because it’s been dead due to stroke, if you can get connections into the deep brain in two different areas, you can imagine adding new cortical areas, just like adding new brain areas entirely — something simply not possible with conventional electrodes. But, I’d say longer term, the long-term mission of the company is to understand how the brain creates the mind and to learn to build engineered brains.”

Hodak went on to note that Science Corporation’s belief is that many people will eventually use some kind of BCI. While the company isn’t designing for “healthy 40-year-olds,” he said, it believes people will eventually need some kind of BCI by the age of 60 or 70.
“We want to figure out how do we extend not just lifespan but health span,” Hodak said.

articles.headline: Pentagon pushes hypersonic weapons production as startups slash costs
keyFacts: The U.S. military is developing hypersonic weapons, though government estimates show traditional models cost up to $70 million per missile.
Startup Castelion is designing hypersonic missiles priced under $500,000 to lower production costs, its chief executive said.
Castelion is building a factory to produce thousands of Blackbeard hypersonic weapons annually for military jets, launchers, and vessels.
body: As the U.S. works to refill its missile stockpile , it is also looking to develop new weapons for its arsenal.

"We're going to need all three tiers of missiles. The cheap ones, the ones that are now the high-end like Patriot and then maybe some hypersonics," said Mark Cancian, a retired U.S. Marines colonel and senior advisor with the CSIS Defense and Security Department.
The U.S. military is taking an increasing interest in hypersonic weapons, which are maneuverable and travel five times faster than the speed of sound.
"These hypersonic systems are now seen as the novel revolutionary system and the ballistic missile is seen as the archaic one," said UC Berkeley Senior Research Scholar Cameron Tracy.
US FALLS BEHIND IN HYPERSONIC RACE AS CHINA, RUSSIA GAIN EDGE

But the weapons the military has traditionally invested in could come at a cost. Estimates from the Government Accountability Office show missiles for the Army’s long-range hypersonic weapon, the Dark Eagle, could cost more than $40 million each. As the Navy works to equip its Zumwalt Destroyers with hypersonics, the GAO puts estimates at $70 million per missile, which includes costs to develop and incorporate the necessary technologies. The GAO also notes the modernization project is two years behind schedule.

"In the long run, for example, the Army thinks that the long-ranged hypersonic weapon will become cheaper as production ramps up," said Xiaodon Liang, arms control association senior policy analyst for Nuclear Weapons Policy and Disarmament.

Tomahawk missiles cost around $2.6 million, according to the U.S. Navy. Army budget documents show Patriot missiles cost nearly $4 million. Precision Strike Missiles or PrSMs cost $1.6 million per unit. The U.S. Navy could buy almost 27 tomahawks for the price of one hypersonic missile aboard the Zumwalt Destroyers. The Army could buy around 25 PrSMs for the price of one Dark Eagle hypersonic weapon.

"The U.S. has invested in recent years in several of the programs that are starting to become into fruition," said Liang. "These are exquisite weapons. And I think that the military is acquiring them for exquisite purposes."

Hypersonic weapons travel up to 20 times faster than traditional missiles and an adversary’s reaction time is thought to be six times shorter. Hypersonic speeds are also vital for both evading enemy defense systems and executing strikes. The Atlantic Council estimates 75% fewer hypersonic weapons would be needed for a mission.
US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES
Startups are hoping to bring down some of the costs to produce hypersonic weapons with more affordable missiles and increased testing capabilities.
"The weapon itself is under $500,000, which, if you know about munitions, that's incredibly cheap," Castelion co-founder and CEO Bryon Hargis said.
The Army and Navy are investing in Castelion's Blackbeard hypersonic weapon , which the company says is designed for mass production.

"It is a story about hypersonics and what they can provide in terms of a weapon, but it's really a story of American manufacturing," Hargis said. "The company is focused on providing America options to have that middle deterrence layer, and we're doing that through production."

This year, Castelion began building what it says will be the largest dedicated hypersonic weapon production factory in the U.S. Project Ranger is expected to produce thousands of Blackbeard weapons annually. Those will eventually be used to fill Castelion’s various contracts, such as integrating the weapons into the U.S. Navy's F/A-18 Super Hornet Jets, incorporating the system into the U.S. Army’s HIMARS and deploying Blackbeard on unmanned surface vessels.

"The advantage of a hypersonic system is that it goes very far, it gets there quickly and it's highly survivable because of that maneuverability. And that's important for achieving deterrence because it's hard to shoot down," Hargis said.
Hypersonic weapons remain mostly in Earth’s atmosphere. The missiles are maneuverable during flight and can strike a target quickly, in 15-30 minutes from around 1,725 miles away.
US REBUILDING WEAPONS STOCKPILE COULD DELAY ORDERS FROM ALLIES

"If you don't know what the target would be initially, unlike a ballistic missile where you can calculate where it'll land, you might misinterpret, for example, an incoming strike as a decapitation attempt. And that would be very concerning," Liang said.
Developers say the U.S. speaks with other countries about missile launches and what the intended targets are. But there are other concerns that hypersonic maneuverability could lead to inaccuracy.

"Technologies do tend to improve over time as testing and especially as experience with use builds up, but there are pretty important physical constraints on the performance of these systems," said Tracy.
Defense contractor Rocket Lab is working with the War Department to improve hypersonic missile capabilities through an increasing number of test launches.
INSIDE AMERICA'S LASER REVOLUTION AS THE MILITARY NEARS BIG BATTLEFIELD BREAKTHROUGH

"With our HASTE program, what we have enabled is low-cost, high-frequency hypersonic and missile defense testing. And when you can say that you can get that cheaper and faster, now you're looking at more of a shots on goal approach to demonstrating capability of the technology insertion cycle," Rocket Lab Vice President of Global Launch Services Brian Rogers said.

Rocket Lab’s HASTE is a suborbital test bed launch vehicle that provides flight test opportunities for the government to advance hypersonic and suborbital system technology development. The vehicle is derived from Rocket Lab’s Electron rocket, which has launched nearly 100 missions.

"Rather than saying we need to be stuck in an analysis environment, and then it's a very rigorous test campaign that costs a lot of money and involves a lot people, now you can say we're planning 12 tests this year. We don't have to bet the farm on any one of them, which allows us to take more risk and really move the needle in terms of technology development," Rogers said.
The U.S. military has never used a hypersonic weapon but has explored deploying its Dark Eagle to the Middle East.

"I would be very surprised if we used them and would be even more surprised if we used it extensively because of the small number of missiles that exist and the concerns already about the munitions stockpile," Liang said.

articles.headline: Raiders' Kirk Cousins gets a boost after being benched against Patriots
keyFacts: The Las Vegas Raiders benched quarterback Kirk Cousins during their game against the New England Patriots to play rookie Fernando Mendoza.
USA Today analyst Elisha Twerski noted that Cousins ranks as fantasy's QB6 and has strong statistics through the first five weeks.
Cousins will face a Buffalo Bills team in Week 6 that has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.
body: It can't feel good to be a veteran quarterback in the NFL and get benched, only able to watch the action on the field from the sidelines, knowing your team isn't' having you be part of the action. Of course, being benched is more complicated than that, and when the Las Vegas Raiders benched Kirk Cousins last weekend during the team's game against the New England Patriots, there was more to it. They wanted to give rookie Fernando Mendoza a chance to take the field.
But the good news is that Week 6 is a fresh week for Cousins and the Raiders, and some stats show that he has a unique chance to shine against the Buffalo Bills.
Kirk Cousins has a chance to bounce back in Week 6

USA Today has released its take on the "risers and sleepers" on each NFL team after the action in Week 5, and one of the risers is Cousins. In the piece, Elisha Twerski of the outlet says not to sleep on him.
"Through five weeks, Cousins ranks as fantasy's QB6," he notes in the piece. "The veteran has thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of five contests and surpassed 240 yards in all but one."
He adds this tidbit: "In Week 6, he'll be taking on a Bills team that's ceded the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks with MNF pending."

So, those who weren't happy to see Cousins benched last week can look ahead and know that he has a real opportunity against the Buffalo Bills. Of course, the Bills are hungry to keep their winning streak going, and they're 4-1 for the season. But Vegas also wants to get above its three wins this season, so expect a competitive game.

- Eagles' Jalen Hurts shouldn't be blamed for loss to Jaguars
- Cowboys get bad news heading into Packers game
- Green Bay Packers get great news after win over Bears

articles.headline: Rams' Alaric Jackson suspended for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb
keyFacts: The NFL suspended Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he punched Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb in the face following a post-game altercation.
The incident occurred after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime victory while players were exchanging jerseys, following trash talk from Chubb directed at Rams players.
Jackson will miss games against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, and he will be eligible to return to the active roster on October 26.
body: The Buffalo Bills picked up one of the wildest wins of the season on Monday night with an overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams, and somehow, things actually got even wilder after the game. Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb and appeared to make contact with his face.

The NFL suspended Jackson two games for the incident. He will be eligible to return to the active roster on Monday, Oct. 26, which sets him up to miss the Week 6 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals and Week 7 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders. His first game back from suspension will be on Nov. 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Following Buffalo's 37-34 win, several players from both teams stayed on the field to do a jersey exchange and that's when the drama started. Jackson was trading his jersey with Buffalo's Deone Walker and while that exchange was going on, Chubb was talking trash to Jackson.

The Rams offensive lineman clearly didn't like what Chubb had to say because he walked straight over to the Bills' pass-rusher and got in his face. Jackson and Chubb then started yelling at each other, and that's when things got ugly.
At that point, the two players had to be separated by their teammates. You can see a video of the incident below.

"After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to 'any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship,'" the NFL said in a statement.
As you can see, Jackson's punch was pretty blatant, and the suspension is unsurprising given the historical precedent for that punishment.

During the 2025 season, Lions safety Brian Branch got hit for instigating a post-game fight following a loss to the Chiefs. That altercation actually took place on Oct. 12, 2025, exactly one year before Jackson's punch.
Jackson was suspended for two games in 2024 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, so this is not his first time standing under the league's watchful eye.
Based on post-game video, it appears that Chubb was talking trash to anyone and everyone.
After he left the field, Chubb was asked about the altercation.
"Just emotions. You know what I mean," Chubb said of what happened, via the California Post. "Emotional game. It was a close game."
In the video, you can see that Chubb put his hand in Jackson's face just before Jackson threw the punch and that may have instigated the situation.
"They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back, so I just chilled," Chubb said.
Chubb was also asked if he was quarreling with anyone specifically and it appears that Jackson wasn't the only Rams player he was talking trash to.
"It was just the whole team," Chubb said.
Chubb finished the game with just two tackles, but his team won and that's what matters.

articles.headline: How long will humans be needed for translation?
keyFacts: Google said people translate one trillion words monthly on Google Translate, amid growing industry adoption of AI translation tools.
Translators warn that AI translation still produces critical errors in legal and medical fields despite sounding natural and fluent.
Researcher François Yvon expects future AI translation systems will evaluate their own work and indicate when they are not sure.
body: - Published
"Il pleut des cordes," say the French when it's raining hard.
"It's raining ropes," is the direct translation. It's the kind of idiom which can trip up an AI translator.
"You can imagine the dilemma this throws AI into," says FranÃ§ois Yvon, a research director specialised in automatic translation with the French National Centre for Scientific Research CNRS.
He says a well-trained system will know that ropes are not literally falling from the sky and use the English phrase "it's raining cats and dogs".
"But is it going to find the equivalent when it's translating into Indonesian?" asks Yvon.
A comment on the weather is pretty low-risk, but more and more translation is being done by machines, and on topics with higher stakes than the weather.
In April, Google said people are now translating, external one trillion words a month with Google Translate.
That doesn't count the others: DeepL, Microsoft, Claude, ChatCGT and Gemini, not to mention made-to-measure corporate translation systems.
Direct sales of machine translation, external (i.e. outside general AI subscriptions) were worth an estimated $1.4bn (Â£1bn) last year.

"For plenty of use cases, raw AI translation is now the right call: multiplying your costs by 100 to catch the last few percent of errors isn't rational if you're translating internal documents or product listings," says John Zimmerman, founder of OKA (Open Knowledge Association), a Swiss non-profit that translates Wikipedia articles into other languages.
"For an encyclopedia it's different. Wikipedia runs on trust. A wrong fact can sit there for years and get cited by journalists and AI systems," he says.

With more than 10,000 published pieces, mostly into Spanish, Portuguese and English, OKA is, Zimmerman says, the single largest contributor of translated articles to the collaborative online encyclopedia.
Which is something it absolutely could not have become without AI.
"Translating 10,000 articles the traditional way would cost millions. In our process, the AI produces the draft, then a human translator checks every sentence," he explains.
But that human input is required less and less.

"The machine output is now good enough that skipping the human entirely has become a serious option, and a real temptation across the industry. Two or three years ago, with tools like DeepL, our translators still rewrote a good chunk of every draft.
"Today the prose often doesn't need fixing at all. So, the question is no longer whether AI translation is good, it clearly is, but whether it's good enough to remove the human," says Zimmerman.
Not yet, translators argue.
Ariella BaltiÃ© is a translator and legal expert specialised in translating court documents from English into French.
She was contacted recently by someone who'd already translated his documents with AI, asking her to check them.
"There were two major errors right at the beginning," she said.
The AI had translated "Le demandeur" (the plaintiff) as "the requester". "Totally awkward for legal papers," says BaltiÃ©.
When the AI saw "Madame X, Ã©pouse Y" (Ms X, wife of Y'), it came up with "Ms X marries Y".
In other words, it mistook a noun for a verb, completely losing the meaning of the phrase.
The consequences of mistranslation in the legal sphere can be serious. In the US, for example, errors in machine-translated asylum applications have led to delays in the release of detainees.
Accuracy is a matter of life and death in the medical field.
"The units for dosages and blood tests often include Greek letters," says Carol Bereuter, who is a specialist in medical translations.
She came across one automatically-translated text that had translated the greek letter Î¼ as milli (one thousandth) instead of micro (one millionth).
"That's a serious error. If you give someone a milligram when it's meant to be a microgram, you are giving them a thousand times the dose," points out Bereuter.
She also makes the point that, as AI translators have got better, catching errors has got more difficult.

"Whereas in the past, with things like Google Translate, the sentence would jump out at you because there'd be a grammatical error or it would sound clunky, today it sounds perfectly legitimate. It sounds fluid. It sounds natural. So the errors are a lot harder to spot."

"If it's something that will bear your signature, there's a risk for your reputation. And if decisions are going to be taken on the basis of a translation concerning a medical procedure, a contract you might sign or a major purchase you might make, the risk is even greater," warns FranÃ§ois Yvon.
Even sentences that seem quite clear to a human can trip up an AI service, he says.

"When you have words with different meanings, it's usually very clear for a human which one applies because they understand the context, but when a machine translator comes across the sentence 'translate into Polish', for example, it is quite capable of deciding it must be all about shoe cream, says Yvon.
Context is often crucial. If an AI translator hasn't grasped that we're talking about a football match it is liable to mis-translate "taking a corner".
Last year OKA ran a study, funded by Wikimedia. It studied 119 articles, 10 language pairs and more than 1,000 hours of translator work.

"27% of the AI-generated text still got corrected before publication. Three quarters of those corrections were errors the AI introduced, and 5 to 6% of errors changed the meaning of the original text," says Zimmerman.
Eradicating those errors is likely to be challenging.
"As things stand, I think the fundamental way these systems function makes it quite hard to imagine how they could become 100% reliable," says FranÃ§ois Yvon.

This is because probability is a crucial part of the way AI translates each word rather than another and what is probably correct is not the same as what is correct. Especially in the realm of something as subtle and surprising as language.
He thinks a new generation of tech will be an improvement.

"We will see translation systems that are increasingly capable of evaluating what they do and correcting themselves using different AI tools simultaneously: one to do the translation, a second to criticize it and a third to produce a new version, for example."
But perhaps the big moment will be when AI can show doubt.
"The real breakthrough won't come until these systems are not merely capable of translating but also of telling us when they're not sure," Yvon says.

articles.headline: Saka responds to Arteta's challenge with 'huge impact'
keyFacts: Bukayo Saka came off the bench despite illness to score a goal and provide an assist in Arsenal's 3-0 Champions League win over Lille.
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta stated before the match that he wants Saka to aim for two or three goals per game.
Arteta said that Saka delivered a huge impact with real quality in response to the scoring challenge set for him.
body: - Published
Bukayo Saka responded to the challenge set by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as he proved a game-changer in the 3-0 Champions League win over Lille.
The England forward has been told he should aim to score "two or three" goals per game - such was his quality and the expectation from his boss.
Saka did not achieve that tally against the French visitors, but shook off illness to come off the bench and assist Eberechi Eze's strike that made it 2-0, before rolling in his side's third goal.
The 25-year-old has now scored four goals in nine games this season and looks to be taking the next step in his evolution as Arsenal's key man.

With the majority of his side's attacking play involving him, he has always been an influential figure. But with opposition defenders doubling up on him and injury issues over the last two seasons, there were doubts over whether Saka could still do what was asked of him in attack or if he had lost a yard of pace.
Arteta has tweaked Saka's positioning this season and, prior to Lille's visit, said it has been done deliberately to get him closer to the goal.
'He delivered with real quality'

"That is where we need to get him," said the Gunners boss before the game. "And if he misses the chance, so be it. At the end, the more volume we generate, the bigger the probability of him scoring more goals."
Saka's strike against Lille was a confident one-touch finish and came after he missed a late one-on-one opportunity in Saturday's Premier League victory over Leeds.
"He has been getting in great positions, getting shots, getting one-touch finishes and tap-ins," added Arteta.

"That is the kind of unpredictability we have with that player, otherwise we know how the opponent is going to defend him. He is doing well, he could have had another four or five goals by now, easily. But if he continues like that, we know.

"When he talks about scoring a certain amount of goals, he needs to be thinking about scoring a certain amount of goals per game. If that shifts, that mentality, he will get into those positions and score more goals."
Saka has scored 20 goals in a season just once in his career, which came in the 2023-24 campaign and 16 in the Premier League.

But the winger has also been in good goalscoring form for England with five in his last four matches and scored a double in the 7-0 Nations League demolition of Croatia in the recent international break.

Saka is now on 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal, only behind Thierry Henry (42), while he has nine assists in the Champions League which puts him behind Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14).
He has refused to disclose the targets he has set himself, but Arteta welcomed Saka's response following his message to do more in front of goal.
The Spaniard said: "I don't know if that's the case, but I am very happy.

"He wasn't feeling that good yesterday and today, as he had some sort of illness. He wasn't ready to start but he was really wanting to contribute to the team if it was needed and he came on and made a huge impact and delivered with real quality."
Arteta revealed he also spoke to Saka after telling the media about his desire for the player to have a greater impact.
"After the press conference... I said 'Bukayo, I just killed you in the press conference, good luck tomorrow'.
"He was laughing. He knows that we have discussed these kind of things and he takes it because he wants to be the best version of himself.
"In order to do that, you have to put big objectives and challenges and try to reason by working and being consistent - and when it doesn't work, keep going because he has the ability to do it."
Gyokeres struggles on mixed night for fringe players
Arteta made five changes to the team that started the win over Leeds as the Gunners looked to navigate six matches in all competitions during this month.
Noni Madueke moved to the right wing after putting in a good performance on the left at the weekend, with Mikel Merino, Eze and Viktor Gyokeres all coming into the starting XI.
Eze had started just two games in all competitions before the match with Lille and Arteta had said his attitude had been "phenomenal" despite a lack of game time.
The 28-year-old showed flashes of his undoubted quality and his finish for Arsenal's second goal - and his first of the season - will give him confidence going forward.
Madueke had a mixed night as he showed his ability to beat a defender, but questions remain over his end product - even if he provided the assist for Jurrien Timber's classy opening goal.
However, it was not a good night for Gyokeres.
The Sweden striker scored 21 goals in all competitions last season as Arsenal won the title for the first time in 22 years and displayed his willingness to run and work hard.
But Gyokeres had just 12 touches before being replaced and Kai Havertz, as he so often does, looked a much better and more natural fit for the Arsenal frontline, teeing up Saka's goal too.

Arteta brought on Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard after going 1-0 up and all three contributed to show why they are still the first names on the teamsheet and why the Arsenal boss will be so reliant on them if they are to achieve more honours.

articles.headline: 11 Magic: The Gathering Marvel Cards That Perfectly Capture Their Characters
keyFacts: Polygon reported that Wizards of the Coast designed Magic: The Gathering crossover cards to translate Marvel characters defining traits into gameplay mechanics.
The article detailed specific card designs, such as Wolverine, Fierce Fighter using a rule to instantly wipe away accumulated damage to simulate his healing factor.
The publication noted that cards like Bruce Banner and Mjölnir used transformations and special equip requirements to reflect the lore of their source material.
body: One of the most interesting things about Magic: The Gathering is how a well-designed card can tell you everything you need to know about a character without requiring a single line of exposition. A clever ability, a specific gameplay restriction, or even a minor mechanical detail can capture what makes a character so memorable, distilling their defining traits into something you can actually experience at the table. When a card’s abilities tell a story that fans already know, the result can be more satisfying than any amount of flavor text.

That’s what makes Universes Beyond, Wizards of the Coast’s line of crossover sets, such a compelling experiment. Bringing beloved characters into Magic is one thing, but translating what makes them special into the game’s mechanics is an entirely different challenge. The game has already drawn from all kinds of fictional worlds, ranging from the post-apocalyptic wasteland of Fallout to the unforgettable adventures of Final Fantasy, each set offering a unique spin on iconic characters, locations, and objects. Some designs reference a memorable moment or character trait, while the best make their mechanics feel inseparable from the source material.

With Marvel Super Heroes bringing the likes of the Avengers, the X-Men, and some of Marvel’s most formidable villains to the battlefield, there are plenty of contenders for the set’s most inspired designs. These are the cards that capture their subjects so perfectly through gameplay that it’s difficult to imagine a better way to represent them.
11 Age of Ultron

Ultron is frightening because he doesn’t see himself as a villain in the ordinary sense, but rather sees humanity as a problem to be solved, and his mechanical nature allows him to pursue that conclusion with a relentless and detached efficiency. While the designers at Wizards translated that threat into simple creatures, like Machine Overlord and Artificial Malovolence, they also crafted Age of Ultron as a five-mana Saga that lets players orchestrate the character’s grand design stage by stage.

The card begins by quietly purging biological life across the table (destroying one nonartifact creature per opponent), rolls straight into mass-producing 2/2 Robot tokens, and culminates in an overwhelming machine march that grants your synthetic forces deathtouch and +1/+1 counters. It’s a rare piece of game design that captures a major comic crossover event — one that would inevitably become its own movie in the MCU — rather than just a single hero or villain. By embedding the narrative arc directly into the card's mechanics, Age of Ultron stands out as one of the most flavorfully-complete enchantments in the Marvel Super Heroes set, better even than The Coming of Galactus.
10 Wolverine, Fierce Fighter

Wolverine has spent decades being stabbed, shot, blasted, and subjected to horrors few others in the Marvel Universe could endure. Magic’s Wolverine, Fierce Fighter, exemplifies that legendary durability by translating his mutant healing factor directly into gameplay mechanics. He enters the battlefield with haste and immediately fights another creature, so Wolverine hurls himself straight into danger the second he lands. The real stroke of brilliance, however, lies in how the card processes incoming damage. While damage normally accumulates throughout a turn in Magic, Wolverine’s rule text specifies that whenever new damage would be dealt to him, all previously marked damage is immediately wiped clean.

It’s an unusual effect that perfectly encapsulates what it feels like to fight Wolverine in the comics. You might hurt him, but putting him down before he recovers is another matter entirely. Swarm strategies and token armies fail to wear him down because each subsequent strike instantly triggers his healing factor, resetting his toughness before the previous wound can take hold. That continuous recovery transforms his healing factor into an active part of combat — one that you can exploit to keep him in play as long as possible. It elevates Logan beyond a standard stat-line, turning him into a relentless berserker who simply refuses to stay down, even when printed into a Magic card.
9 Avengers Tower

The Avengers are at their best when a collection of wildly different heroes come together to solve a problem none of them could handle alone, which is kind of what the colorless land Avengers Tower is trying to emulate. Designed to function as the ultimate rally point, the card tap-filters mana specifically to help you cast diverse Hero spells and features an activated ability that lets you dig into your library to recruit fresh teammates when the team is stretched thin.

That focus on thematic infrastructure makes Avengers Tower a 10/10 Marvel card, standing as a high point in how the set translates iconic locations into functional game mechanics. Much like Castle Doom, which rewards ruthless play by pumping out Doombot tokens, or Villainous Hideout, these land cards turn comic book geography into active tactical hubs. By grounding the gameplay directly in the settings where these stories unfold, the design team ensured that even the real estate in the Marvel Super Heroes set feels deeply rooted in lore that resonates on the battlefield.
8 Storm, Force of Nature

Storm is one of the most powerful mutants in the Marvel Universe, capable of manipulating weather on a scale that can make entire armies look helpless. Storm, Force of Nature, expresses that power through a clever meta-nod: whenever she deals combat damage to a player, she grants the infamous Storm mechanic to the next instant or sorcery spell you cast that turn. It’s a brilliant fusion of game lore and comic lore. As an Omega-level mutant, Ororo doesn't just strike once; she alters the global conditions of the battlefield, causing every spell that follows her assault to duplicate rapidly like a cascading tempest.

Though technically released in the limited-edition Secret Lair x Marvel superdrop rather than the main Marvel Super Heroes booster set, her design still achieves that 10/10 "no notes" flavor standard. By tying her character directly to one of Magic’s most notorious mechanics, which shares her very name, the designers crafted a legendary card that feels instantly iconic.
7 Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor

Mjölnir operates on one of the most sacred rules in all of Marvel lore: Thor’s hammer can only be lifted by those deemed worthy. Magic: The Gathering directly encoded that into Mjölnir, Hammer of Thor, which features a specialized “Equip worthy” mechanic. By defining worthiness as a legendary non-Villain creature with red or white in its color identity, the card prevents players from handing the Uru hammer to just any brute with high attack stats. Equipping Mjölnir becomes a genuine test of character on the board rather than a routine gear swap, doubling all damage dealt by the chosen champion while dealing a thunderous four-damage strike the moment it enters play.

That mechanical check makes for some flavorful design. In a game where Equipment artifacts are traditionally passed around freely between random tokens and monsters, restricting Mjölnir respects the core spirit of the source material. The hammer isn’t merely a stat booster; it is a sacred tool that actively judges the creature attempting to wield it. That’s the kind of subtle design choice that turns a fun crossover card into a perfect piece of mechanical storytelling.
6 Bruce Banner // The Incredible Hulk

Few Marvel characters are as defined by the tension between their two identities as Bruce Banner and the Hulk. The double-faced Magic card called Bruce Banner makes that internal conflict literal. On the front face, Banner enters as a fragile 1/1 Human Scientist who taps to draw cards, representing his intellect, caution, and methodical approach to solving problems. Once pushed to the edge, an activated ability (or simply casting him on that side for the same cost) transforms him into The Incredible Hulk, an overwhelming 8/8 force equipped with reach and trample.

The design shines brightest in how it handles his green rage on the battlefield. Through his Enrage trigger, taking damage puts a +1/+1 counter on him, untaps him mid-attack, and immediately grants an additional combat phase to keep swinging. The very essence of the character is written into the transformation from a mild-mannered scientist into an escalating, uncontrollable threat. The card forces you to weigh Bruce's careful utility against the exact right moment to let the monster out of its cage.
5 Doctor Doom, King of Latveria

Doctor Doom is a villain who regards himself as the rightful ruler of the world, and his Magic card gives that arrogance a suitably political edge. Doctor Doom, King of Latveria turns discarded land cards into direct life loss for every opponent, making even the resources you throw away part of his campaign to dominate the table. More tellingly, at the beginning of combat on your turn, he can grant another one of your Villains menace and make it connive, allowing it to grow stronger while Doom directs the action safely from behind the scenes.

That is a pitch-perfect fit for a character who rarely needs to get his own hands dirty when he can manipulate others into doing his bidding. The card avoids reducing Doom to a mindless bruiser tearing up the turf. Instead, it portrays a calculating sovereign who turns every tactical decision and discarded card into an opportunity to consolidate absolute power, something that will likely be on full display in Avengers: Doomsday.
4 Captain America, Living Legend

Captain America has always been far more than just a super-soldier, acting instead almost like a living symbol of perseverance. This is a hero who keeps showing up to fight even when the world has completely changed around him. In sort of the same way, Captain America, Living Legend translates that inspirational ethos into a clever design trick. Not only does he have vigilance, meaning he doesn't need to tap when he attacks, but whenever any of your creatures becomes tapped for the first time during your turn, his presence immediately untaps it.

The card’s secondary rule makes it feel as though Cap is rallying the entire team back on their feet, setting up allies to attack or use tap abilities without ever leaving themselves exposed. It serves as a neat mechanical expression of a hero whose greatest strength has always been his ability to lift everyone up around him, whether by speech, strength, or sheer will. The card's flavor text drives that emotional point home, reminding opponents that even after the world moves on, Steve Rogers will always have a reason to keep fighting.
3 Molecule Man

Molecule Man is one of Marvel’s most absurdly powerful entities, a figure whose total mastery over physical matter puts him in a league entirely his own. This is another Marvel character that could easily come in and wreak havoc on the game of Magic, but his card is rather tame compared to the multiversal destruction he’s capable of in the comics. Magic communicates his reality-warping scale through a deceptively simple rule text that grants every nonland card in your hand Miracle, allowing you to cast spells for zero mana the exact moment you draw them as your first card of the turn.

The effect is wonderfully chaotic, making your hand feel less like a rigid collection of resources and more like a malleable fabric that can be rewritten on a whim. It's the type of design choice that captures his unique place in the lore without making him game-breaking.
2 The Mind Stone

The Infinity Stones stand among some of the most terrifying objects in the entire Marvel Universe, meaning any card representing one such artifact needs to do far more than just provide a minor resource boost. That’s where The Mind Stone comes in, beginning its life as an indestructible artifact capable of generating white mana before its true, mind-bending power unlocks once you pay the resources required to harness it. After a five-mana cost activation, its infinity ability lets you blink another nonland permanent you control at the beginning of your end step, sort of like a Teleportation Circle or Conjurer’s Closet.

While that might initially sound like a modest utility trick, it opens up a massive array of strategic possibilities, letting you endlessly reuse powerful enter-the-battlefield triggers or shield a valuable asset from incoming destruction. Thematically, it offers a brilliant interpretation of the Stone's true capabilities. Rather than simply making its controller physically stronger, it grants them some control over their own bodies in play, turning the battlefield into a shifting puzzle box they can rearrange at will.

articles.headline: Cornell suspends frat parties after gang rape case
keyFacts: Cornell University suspended all fraternity house parties until the end of the 2026/27 academic year, the university announced.
The suspension follows a lawsuit alleging Chi Phi fraternity members drugged and sexually assaulted a woman in October 2024.
New York Attorney General Letitia James is now investigating the case, and Sally Yates will review Cornell's response.
body: Cornell University has suspended all parties at frat houses until the end of the 2026/27 academic year, the university announced on Tuesday.

This comes after the case in which a woman alleged to have been drugged and sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024, with the university's reaction to the gang rape allegations now attracting criticizm from around the nation and overseas.
The new measures include a new "zero tolerance" policy for violations, which would result in an immediate suspension of a chapter.

University President Michael Kotlikoff said these measures were to "provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life" at Cornell, while also determining how it can safely continue. The university has more than 20 active fraternities that are organized under its Interfraternity Council.
It is not clear whether the suspension also includes parties that take place outside the campus.
More support for victims

As part of the measures, Cornell is to hold talks with students and faculty experts about the "the development of safe social alternatives" to Greek life party culture, as well as investing the money needed to support the initiatives' establishment, Kotlikoff said.
The Cornell president also said the institution will be adding a case manager to its Office of Civil Rights to support people that report sexual misconduct to help in navigating the process.

Campus police, which has full law enforcement authority but is controlled by Cornell, are largely the ones responsible for looking into crimes committed at the university. However, Kotlikoff announced that Cornell will work closely with New York State Police to allow an investigation independent of the school.
Decision not to prosecute criticized

The 2024 gang rape allegations were initially investigated by the campus police, which then passed its initial findings to the Tompkins County district attorney, who did not prosecute — a decision that was lader met with widespread criticizm.
The woman filed a lawsuit in September, in which she claimed she had been drugged and sexually assaulted by several fraternity members after attending a party at the Chi Phi house in October 2024.
According to the lawsuit, messages saying she was sexually available were sent among fraternity members without her knowledge.
After learning about the case, Cornell closed the fraternity chapter and disciplined several students, without any criminal charges being filed.
All seven men mentioned in the lawsuit have denied the allegations.

After the case was made public and triggered wide-scale criticism, the investigation is now in the hands of New York Attorney General Letitia James. The university's response will be reviewed by former Deputy US Attorney General Sally Yates.

articles.headline: Manchester United’s Martinez blasts board’s lack of investment
keyFacts: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez criticized the club's board and technical director for a perceived lack of summer squad investment.
The remarks followed a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, extending Manchester United's winless streak to five matches across all competitions.
Former striker Wayne Rooney stated Martinez went too far, while manager Michael Carrick attributed the comments to post-match emotions.
body: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez blasted the club’s board for a perceived lack of investment this summer, after the team were beaten by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday.
United are winless in five games across all competitions after the 2-0 defeat in the Spanish capital and have made their worst start to a league season in 40 years.
“Really poor,” Martinez told Amazon Prime when asked about the team’s performance against Atletico.
“I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection… [or] mirror of how our club is at the moment.”
Martinez said he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad over the summer after United finished third in the Premier League last season and returned to Europe’s top competition.

“I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox], I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for these kind of nights,” he continued.
Martinez said last season the club had “created the base to create an amazing team”, but they did not follow through.
Pressure is mounting on coach Michael Carrick after five games without a win, but Martinez suggested sacking the Englishman was not the way forward.
“You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can’t say more,” said Martinez.
“Tonight it is easy to say the coach [is to blame], easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.”
Red Devils minority owner Jim Ratcliffe was at the stadium to watch the league-phase defeat by last season’s semi-finalists.

Man United spent around 140 million pounds ($185m) this summer on midfielders Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, but fans were upset the club did not reinforce other positions, including left-back and striker.
Speaking to reporters after the game, Carrick said he had not heard Martinez’s comments and so could not judge them.
“I think it’s a little bit on the emotions of the game as well, of coming here and being disappointed not to get something from the game,” said the coach.
Former Manchester United and England striker Wayne Rooney said Martinez’s criticism was excessive.
“I think he’s maybe gone a bit too far, and that should have stayed internal,” Rooney told Amazon Prime.
“You can clearly see that he cares and he wants the club to invest more money in more players, and to do that he’s probably one of the players who’ll be out the door if I’m being honest.”
