articles.headline: Trump allies think Kimberly Guilfoyle’s ‘hope’ for a pardon will keep her from lashing out
keyFacts: President Trump ousted Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle over allegations she solicited money for favors and accepted gifted travel.
Sources told The Post that Guilfoyle is unlikely to criticize Trump because she may need a presidential pardon.
A source said Guilfoyle will likely face a grueling criminal investigation and substantial legal fees regarding her conduct.
body: WASHINGTON — President Trump’s just-ousted ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, known for her diva demands and emotional outbursts, is unlikely to lash out at President Trump and his family because she may need a pardon over the scandal that forced her from office, sources told The Post.

“She’s gonna need a pardon and if she doesn’t behave she ain’t getting one,” a person close to the White House and Trump family said shortly after Trump demanded — and received — her resignation following allegations that she solicited money for favors and received gifted travel from Greek businessmen.
“If I were her, I’d probably shut up and hope for it,” said a second person close to the White House.

Guilfoyle dated Donald Trump Jr. between early 2018 and late 2024, giving her a rare glimpse into the Trump family’s most private conversations and dealings — and making her a potential star witness against the president if congressional Democrats win the midterms on Nov. 3.
The president distanced himself from Guilfoyle Tuesday afternoon, telling reporters: “She wasn’t a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago.”
Guilfoyle denied wrongdoing in her farewell statement.

“These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity,” Guilfoyle wrote. “I have dedicated my professional life to fighting for justice, standing up for what is right, and defending the values that make America exceptional. I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service.”

Trump nominated Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece shortly after the end of her engagement to the first son in what one person close to the family called a “soft landing,” before she went on to engage in conduct that the president decided crossed the line.

There’s unlikely to be another soft landing after she was ousted from her diplomatic post, sources said, with the best she can hope for being clemency that heads off the ruinous legal bills from criminal investigations and possible legal penalties.
A third source close to the White House and familiar with Guilfoyle’s record agreed that a pardon might keep her in line — but described her boisterous personality as difficult to contain.
“Kim is a well-known and world-class fabulist. She is definitely emotional… and could also just say a bunch of crazy stuff,” this person said.
“There is a presumption she has all this dirt that honestly she doesn’t,” he insisted. “It’s Kim, so she can make stuff up obviously, but she’s not exactly a reliable narrator.”

The facts behind the cascading controversies linked to her diplomatic role remain murky, and although she mounted little public defense, her allies have offered explanations for some of her seemingly shady conduct, such as allegedly asking businessman Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 credit card bill in exchange for favors.
Guilfoyle has told people the money was an unpaid speaking fee, and it’s unclear how the lack of payment would impact her legal liability.

It’s also unclear to what extent her allegedly self-described free luxury travel from foreign tycoons intersected with her government role, and whether she ever made good on reported pledges to make people who assisted her wealthy.
However, the process of undergoing a criminal investigation can be grueling.

“Whatever the case, it certainly will be looked at, which would likely be a huge process and a lot of legal fees,” the second source said, noting “she knows well from Jan. 6” the punishing nature of criminal investigations.
Guilfoyle, who is the ex-wife of Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-Calif.), committed much of her resignation statement to pledging continued loyalty to Trump.

“While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end,” she wrote, concluding her statement: “God bless President Trump, God bless our incredible diplomats and service members, and God bless the United States of America.”

articles.headline: Martin Shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharma ban, FTC says
keyFacts: The FTC and seven states asked a federal judge to hold Martin Shkreli in contempt for allegedly violating his lifetime pharmaceutical industry ban.
Officials alleged that Shkreli violated the ban by trading drug company stocks and discussing the industry during social media livestreams.
Regulators asked the court to make Shkreli divest his pharmaceutical stocks, forfeit trading profits, and face escalating future consequences.
body: Martin Shkreli—the ex-pharmaceutical executive infamous for illegally hiking the price of a lifesaving anti-parasitic drug by more than 4,000 percent and getting a seven-year prison sentence for the fraudulent scheme he used to do it—has been under a lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry since 2022.

However, according to the Federal Trade Commission and the attorneys general of seven states, Shkreli has “flagrantly and repeatedly” violated that ban nearly the entire time—allegedly by trading stock in dozens of drug companies and discussing the industry during livestreams on social media.

On Tuesday, the FTC and the seven states asked a federal judge to hold Shkreli in contempt for the alleged violations. The states include New York, California, Illinois, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Virginia—the same states that joined the FTC in suing Shkreli in 2020 over the “elaborate anticompetitive scheme” involving the anti-parasitic drug, Daraprim. The scheme raised the price from $17.50 per pill to $750 per pill virtually overnight, while blocking generic competitors from entering the market.
“Egregious” conduct

In 2022, the federal court recognized the “seriousness” of issuing such a lifetime industry ban, but ruled that “Shkreli’s egregious, deliberate, repetitive, long-running, and ultimately dangerous illegal conduct warrants imposition of an injunction of this scope.” The ban, among many things, “explicitly prohibits” Shkreli from owning stock in pharmaceutical companies and making public statements that could influence a pharmaceutical company’s business, according to the FTC and the states.

With the alleged violations, the FTC and the states are now seeking to force Shkreli to divest from all pharmaceutical companies and pay a fine equal to his profits from trading pharmaceutical company stocks. They also want the court to lay out “clear and escalating consequences” if Shkreli violates the ban in the future, including further financial penalties and incarceration.

articles.headline: Can Vibe Coded Apps Replace Adobe and Microsoft? These AI Apps Hope So
keyFacts: Software engineer Brandon Thomas released 13 free, open-source apps designed to replicate core features of Adobe and Microsoft programs.
These apps offer alternatives to expensive subscriptions, though a CNET expert warned that sharing vibe-coded tools can create legal challenges.
Under a federal settlement agreement, Adobe will pay a $75 million civil penalty and provide $75 million in services to affected users.
body: In this current era of vibe coding — using AI to create mobile and desktop apps — it was probably only a matter of time until someone made free versions of popular apps. That happened this month when a Reddit user announced that he did so with popular but expensive Adobe and Microsoft programs.

The person behind the project is Brandon Thomas, a software engineer who uses the handle “u/ai_art_is_art” on Reddit, where the tools first caught AI enthusiasts’ attention. Thomas has released 13 free, open-source apps on his website, called ArtCraft. These apps aim to replicate the core functionalities of Adobe and Microsoft programs, including Photoshop, Word and PowerPoint — or, as Thomas calls them, PhotoCraft, WordCraft and DeckCraft.

Vibe coding has taken off for software developers and AI enthusiasts, leading to AI-made apps flooding Apple and Google’s app stores. However, significant concerns persist about the overall usefulness, security and long-term viability of vibe-coded apps. Apple removed some apps that help people vibe code this year because the apps didn’t comply with Apple’s developer rules.
More from CNET

But in the US’s current affordability crisis — and with legacy tech companies constantly raising their prices — a cheaper, AI-created alternative to Photoshop or Microsoft Word can be an attractive option for a subscription-weary consumer.

This certainly isn’t the first time a startup has tried to compete with legacy software companies like Adobe and Microsoft. Canva, Affinity and CapCut are extremely popular Adobe alternatives for content creation and editing. Google and Apple each have their own versions of Microsoft’s core business apps.

But ArtCraft’s vibe-coded apps and other potential AI-made apps allow individual users to avoid handing over their cash and data to a major tech company. Using an open-source AI model on your own device, for example, gives you more control over your data than using a cloud-based app through a subscription.
As with all apps, CNET recommends you inspect the privacy and safety policies before using them. This is especially important for vibe-coded apps.

“Vibe coding can make it super easy to swap out old software tools, but it’s legally questionable,” said CNET’s Blake Stimac, a vibe coding expert. “What works great for you as a quick fix could easily turn into a legal battlefield the second you try to share it with the world.”
Representatives for ArtCraft and Adobe did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Microsoft declined to comment.
Will vibe coding kill legacy software?

It’s unlikely that vibe-coded apps will be the sole downfall of legacy software companies like Adobe and Microsoft. But they do highlight the growing frustration with those companies, particularly as subscriptions become even more expensive and their programs become bloated with AI features.

In March, Adobe reached a $150 million settlement with the US government to resolve a federal lawsuit alleging that the software giant trapped consumers in subscription plans with hidden fees and an intentionally convoluted cancellation process. Under the terms of the agreement, Adobe will pay a $75 million civil penalty and provide $75 million in free services to affected users, though the company continues to deny any wrongdoing.

Microsoft has embedded its Copilot AI throughout its software ecosystem, despite notable user backlash. While the company recently removed a few Windows AI features due to negative feedback, it is still plowing ahead with billions of dollars in AI development.

The appeal of ArtCraft and other open-source vibe-coded apps is their ability to let individuals customize programs and avoid hefty subscriptions. The pitch is tailor-made for tech enthusiasts: If you only need limited access to these programs and can set them up yourself for free, why would you pay for Adobe Creative Cloud or Microsoft Office?

But that certainly won’t be the case for everyone. For one, many folks won’t want to take the time to figure out how to download and configure an open-source AI app. Meanwhile, businesses and professional creators will likely prefer the safety and privacy guarantees that Adobe and Microsoft offer, even if they aren’t always ironclad. Better the devil you know…

articles.headline: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser says he 'failed' with Max Payne 3, and I'm sorry Danno but that's just plain wrong
keyFacts: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser stated in an interview that Max Payne 3 was a failure due to negative consensus at the time.
Houser attributed the game's perceived failure to his own writing and the public missing original creator Sam Lake's work.
Publisher Take-Two Interactive stated in 2012 that sales of Max Payne 3 were lower than expected.
body: Dan Houser is a co-founder of Rockstar Games and so I would never presume to tell him he's wrong about any of the games Rockstar has made—except in this one particular instance, where I feel obligated to step up and say, 'Dan, I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.'

The game in question is Max Payne 3, on which Houser played a central role, and one he seems rather down on: In an interview with IGN, he said the game was a "failure" because, simply put, he's not Sam Lake, the Remedy creative director who wrote the first two Max Payne games.

As a very linear game, Max Payne 3 "was a little different" from the open world GTA games he was accustomed to, Houser said, but he also really enjoyed the experience. "I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen.
Alas, he continued, "I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it.

"So I got that completely wrong," Houser said. "I know Sam Lake well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success.

"The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing."

Max Payne 3 is a really interesting case study because it's very much a Max Payne game—grim and gritty, filled with bullet time, body drops, and snappy commentary about how much life sucks—but it's also a full-on Rockstar game, and thus a very different vibe from the previous two entries in the series. Fans who were expecting more of the same—or insisting on it, really—were bound to be disappointed.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But Max Payne 3 itself is nothing short of a brilliant, powerhouse cinematic shooter. It really does feel like "a 12-hour movie," powered by lush cut scenes, a brilliant soundtrack by industrial rock group Health, and great performances across the board, in particular from James McCaffrey in the title role.
With all due respect to Remedy, this is where McCaffrey really hit his stride, digging deep to deliver some truly great lines:
- I wouldn't know right from wrong if one of them was helping the poor and the other was banging my sister.
- Look at me, I'm standing in a nightclub, listening to music I can't stand, I'm five thousand miles from home, I'm armed, and I'm drinking. You don't want to listen to advice from me, amigo.
- I had a hole in my second favourite drinking arm, and the only way we were likely to get Fabiana back now was in instalments.

- I'd killed more cops than cholesterol and still no sign of Becker. It wasn't the first time it dawned on me I should probably have gone over the plan in more detail, but it was too late for that now.
- I was a dumb American in a place where dumb Americans are less popular than the clap.
- I'd put a big shit-eating grin on my face and let these assholes take turns trying to kill me. That's my style and it's too late in the day to hope for change.

- We'd half destroyed Sao Paulo's most hallowed place of worship. Looking back it was strange how the cops never showed up. But things had a habit of only making sense to me looking back, long after I'd run out of time to fix them.
- I'd been sitting at the bar for three hours, or about five years, depending on how you looked at things. I tried not to look at things.

It is fair to say that Max Payne 3 wasn't a massive commercial success: In 2012, publisher Take-Two Interactive said sales of the game came in "lower than expected," resulting in a significantly increased net loss for the quarter. But that's hardly the only measure of success, and I think it's notable that Take-Two said the same, at the same time, about Spec Ops: The Line, a game widely heralded, then and now, for its daring, subversive narrative.

Max Payne 3 was a slower burn, but I think the passage of time has given us a far better perspective on what Rockstar actually delivered: As former PC Gamer writer Andy Kelly wrote a full decade ago, "Over the years I’ve developed a greater appreciation for the risks Rockstar took in breaking Remedy’s established, and beloved, mould."

"It’s a radical departure, but it works," the other Andy wrote in his very correct take on Max Payne 3. "It’s always interesting to see a familiar character thrust into an unfamiliar situation, and Max is hilariously out of place in Brazil. As if being a white American in a favela didn’t draw enough unwanted attention, he makes his life even more difficult by wearing the loudest Hawaiian shirt imaginable. He was comfortable in New York, but here he’s an outsider, and the game plays up to it brilliantly."

And so, Dan, with all due respect, I have to say, 'I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.' Max Payne 3 may have been divisive in its time, and it may not have been the big hit you were hoping for, but I sure wouldn't call it a failure. I'd say Rockstar, and you, absolutely nailed it.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

articles.headline: Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
keyFacts: Apple released an advertisement for its new HomeView smart display that depicts a chaotic morning routine for a family of five.
While tech analyst Benedict Evans found the ad stressful, parents and editor Bridget Carey described it as an accurate depiction of real mornings.
The device's real test will happen when it enters households to determine whether families use the shared display instead of individual phones.
body: Apple’s ad introducing its new HomeView smart display is a little unusual. It’s fast-paced and unruly, depicting a family of five as they rush through the morning routine. There’s yelling and mess, misplaced keys and discarded eggshells. Apple’s typical vibe is clean, simple, orderly; this commercial is chaos.
Apple’s HomeView ad is confusing to everyone except parents
The chaos is surprisingly real for an Apple commercial.
But the spot has parents — those with teen children in particular — feeling seen.

I’ll admit that it stressed me out the first time I watched it, too. Mornings getting my five-year-old out the door are a special breed of chaos, and usually culminate in us playing whatever ad-libbed game will get him to put his shoes on. But it’s not quite as intense as this one, which features dad making French toast, mom losing and finding keys in her pocket, a proxy battle over the thermostat, a teenage boy helping himself to whipped cream from a can, and an unexpected video call. There’s also a microdrama about the daughter’s ride to school with a boyfriend nobody knew about that ends with everyone gathered around the HomeView watching the security camera feed of the two of them departing the porch. It’s a lot for just over three minutes of screentime.

If I know anything, though, I know to trust my colleague Jen Tuohy, senior reviewer and parent to two teens, on matters of the home. Her take? “The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone.”

Other parents of teens shared similar reactions on Threads. When tech analyst Benedict Evans posted about the ad feeling stressful and confusing, CNET editor at large Bridget Carey chimed in to defend it, saying “It was exactly what my morning is like and it was the most real ad I’ve ever seen from Apple.” Others agreed, saying it “accurately captured” real life and that it “hit home,” no pun intended, at least I think.

Even if Apple didn’t need to do much to heighten the stakes of a family getting out the door, there is of course plenty of sleight of hand at work when it comes to making the HomeView appear so essential. The family has seemingly drilled a hole directly into the middle of their kitchen island to accommodate the charging cable, for one. And what sibling is going to check a text message from a secret boyfriend on the communal kitchen screen with their brother sitting at arm’s length? I don’t believe any teenager trusts Apple’s privacy features that far.

The confusion about the commercial is understandable. This is a far cry from the quiet luxury lifestyle everyone seems to enjoy in Apple’s Vision Pro ads. There’s also Evans’ observation that the HomeView doesn’t really solve any of the problems that come up throughout the course of the video. In the case of a spontaneous FaceTime call from the grandparents, the screen in the middle of the kitchen seems to make things worse.

But maybe morning chaos isn’t the problem that’s being solved. If the alternative is five people all interacting with their own phones, then the HomeView presents a different picture where everyone gets the essential information they need from one shared screen and stays more present.

A screen that makes you be more present is a lovely idea, but the real test will come when it’s in real households. Is the HomeView going to be enough to convince families to put their personal devices down? Will everyone just ignore it and keep scrolling on their own iPhones? These are questions worth answering before you start drilling holes in your kitchen island! In any case, an ungovernable morning routine is probably a feature of a busy household, not a bug. Just ask a parent.

articles.headline: New Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Called Her Husband… What?!
keyFacts: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia mistakenly called her husband 'my president' during her first press conference.
Zacharia, who succeeded Karoline Leavitt, ended the 14-minute press conference shortly after acknowledging the verbal slip-up.
An anonymous White House official told MS NOW that Zacharia needs to get much better fast.
body: This feels akin to a kid accidentally calling their teacher “mom.”
On Tuesday, new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia stood behind the podium at the White House for the very first time, and it was a mess.

Karoline Leavitt’s successor made an unpolished debut that lasted about 14 minutes, mostly spent looking down as she read from a prepared statement, anxiously playing with her hair and stumbling over her words.
At the tail end of her press conference, however, she had one moment that was significantly more cringe-inducing than anything that preceded it.
It began when Zacharia was asked how she manages being a working mother of four kids.
“Well, first of all, I want to give my husband an amazing shout-out,” Zacharia began. “We have four kids ranging from [ages] 12, 10, 8 and 6 — three of them are boys, so we have a handful.”
She then tried to explain that her husband and children were in Washington, D.C., with her to celebrate a few family birthdays as a unit. That’s when her epic verbal slip-up emerged.

“I love being with my kids — the idea of not spending evenings with my kid, kids is completely unacceptable, so my president—or excuse me, my husband,” Zacharia said. She immediately recognized her mistake.
“Uh, that’s a good one,” she said nervously, then rambled a bit more before abruptly shutting down the press conference.
One X user summed up the general vibe of Zacharia’s gaffe pretty accurately.
Although Fox News tried to give Zacharia’s debut a rosy spin, an anonymous White House official told MS NOW it was noteworthy for all the wrong reasons.

“Getting behind the podium is tough, but she got off on the wrong foot. She needs to get much better fast, otherwise she’ll break Scaramucci’s record,” the anonymous source said, referring to former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci, who was only in his role for 10 days during President Donald Trump’s first term.

articles.headline: Harry Kane overtakes Lionel Messi in stunning Champions League feat as he chases Cristiano Ronaldo streak
keyFacts: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane scored twice in a 3-3 draw against Viking, surpassing Lionel Messi's record of Champions League goals scored after the age of 30.
Kane has now scored in nine successive games, putting him in a position to potentially chase Cristiano Ronaldo's record of 11 consecutive goals.
Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund stated that contract extension discussions with Kane are going well and he feels comfortable at the club.
body: Harry Kane has impressively overtaken Lionel Messi for Champions League goals scored over the age of 30 in fewer games.
The striker netted twice in Bayern Munich ’s entertaining 3-3 draw at Norwegian side Viking on Tuesday evening.
Harry Kane fired scored twice for Bayern in a 3-3 draw against Viking and moved past Messi’s tally for Champions League goals after 30 Getty
Trailing 2-0 at the interval, Kane inspired Bayern to a comeback, scoring twice while playing a key role in his side’s third before they unfortunately conceded late on.
Kane’s first came from the penalty spot in the 54th minute and the England captain only had to wait a further six minutes to grab his second of the evening.
And it was that goal that took his tally to 36 goals in 40 games after the age of 30.
Kane, now 33, has bolstered his account since arriving in Bavaria in 2023, so much so that he has now eclipsed Messi ’s total.
The Argentine netted 35 goals in 48 games beyond his 30th birthday.
That shows the magnitude of Kane’s prowess in recent years while providing a ringing endorsement for his recent Ballon d’Or nomination .
Kane’s double means he has now scored for nine successive games to equal Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy ‘s record.
And now Cristiano Ronaldo ’s record of 11 goals in succession is firmly in his sights ahead of the visit of Arsenal to the Allianz Arena next week, live on talkSPORT.
Should get on the scoresheet against the Gunners, Kane’s opportunity to equal Rona l do will come in the trip to Atletico Madrid next month.
Kane’s season at a glance
The striker is now up to eight goals for the season while registering four assists in his nine appearances.
Kane has now surpassed Messi’s tally and is also chasing Cristiano Ronaldo’s record
He is also now eyeing Ronaldo’s feat of 11 consecutive goals after scoring in his ninth straight European game Getty
Kane kicked off the season in style with three goals and three assists in five first five Bundesliga outings.
His brilliance has spilled onto the international scene with Kane having achieved his 125th cap for England, matching Peter Shilton ‘s all-time national appearance record.
He scored six times in England’s four matches during the recent international break, taking his tally to 91 goals for the Three Lions.
Kane’s contract with Bayern expires next summer but negotiations are on going over a two-year extension .
Bayern Munich sporting director Christoph Freund said on Friday that he is ‘very positive’ about discussions with Kane who himself has expressed his desire to remain at the club.
“There are always scenarios as long as it’s not signed,” Freund said. “There’s no new development.
Kane’s goals fired Bayern to a league and cup double as he scored 61 times for the club last season Getty
“The talks are going well. We’re very positive, everyone knows we’re determined to extend his contract and Harry feels very comfortable here.”
Since his arrival from Tottenham, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 154 appearances.
He has scooped the Bundesliga Golden Boot in each of his three seasons, whilst firing Bayern to two Bundesliga titles.

articles.headline: Famous And Innovative Duke Nukem, Quake Level Designer ‘Levelord’ Has Died
keyFacts: Video game level designer Richard Gray, known as Levelord, has reportedly died at age 68.
Gray created popular maps for games including Duke Nukem 3D, Quake, and Sin, and co-founded Ritual Entertainment.
Colleagues and companies like Apogee Entertainment paid tribute to Gray following his passing.
body: Richard ‘Levelord’ Gray has reportedly died, according to Apogee Entertainment and individuals who were close to the legendary and beloved level designer who helped create fan-favorite maps in games like Duke Nukem 3D, Quake, and Sin.

Gray, known online by his mapping handle Levelord, explained in a 2016 interview that he didn’t really start making maps in games like Doom until he was 35. He later joined the Duke Nukem 3D team in his 40s, relatively late compared to most other game devs working on shooters in the ’90s and early 2000s. After that, he left and formed his own studio, which would eventually become Ritual Entertainment. That team worked on Quake’s first mission pack, Scourge of Armagon, Sin, Star Trek: Elite Force 2, and Counter-Strike: Condition Zero, among other games.

While working on the Quake mission pack at Ritual, Gray created “The Edge of Oblivion,” the third and last secret level of Scourge of Armagon. This level is credited by many as being the first “islands in space” or “platform in the void” type of FPS map. That style of map would become extremely popular in later FPS games like Unreal Tournament and Quake 3 Arena. Levelord also designed the MP map “Behind Zee Bookcase” in Sin, which is often credited as one of the first examples of a 3D FPS level designed to make you feel like you were the size of a small mouse exploring a real-world environment.

And of course, during his time developing levels in Duke Nukem 3D, he became famous for his hidden Easter egg messages tucked away in a part of the map that you could only reach using cheats. If you did, you’d find a message from Levelord: “You’re not supposed to be here.”
In 2016, when asked how he could be sure that players would even find the now-famous secret, Gray told Duke64Nukem.com:

Did we give you the cheat codes to find easily? Then, of course, most all of you would be flying around, seeing what you could break, find easter eggs the easy way â¦bingo! I gave you an easter egg that you had to cheat to find.
On Tuesday, devs who worked with Gray posted about the legendary developer in the wake of his passing.

“Devastating news today,” shared Doom co-creator and developer John Romero. “Richard ‘Levelord’ Gray was such a great guy. Like many of our friends, I wish I could have hung out with him again. He was full of life, a gentle soul, and an excellent level designer. He was called ‘Levelord’ for a reason.”
We are deeply saddened by the passing of Richard âLevelordâ Gray.
From his legendary work on Duke Nukem 3D to the countless players and developers he inspired, Richard leaves behind a lasting legacy.
Rest in peace, Levelord. pic.twitter.com/UZPWoM04XY
— Apogee Entertainment (@Apogee_Ent) October 13, 2026

“A heartbreaking day. Richard was a stellar talent who joined the game industry in his 40s when Apogee hired him to join the Duke 3D team,” posted Apogee founder Scott Miller. “He was a relentless hard worker, a fun teammate, and an overall great human. His levels in Duke Nukem 3D and Sin will live on forever. And Richard created one of the best easter eggs in gaming history: ‘You’re not supposed to be here! — Levelord.’ RIP.”

Fellow 3D Realms/Apogee Software developer Joe Siegler explained on social media that he heard the news from Gray’s wife and mentioned that the level designer had dealt with cancer over the years, though no cause of death has been officially confirmed yet.

“We worked together back at Apogee/3DR for a few years mostly on Duke Nukem 3D,” said Siegler. “Such a fun time in my life. We stayed in touch long after he left to found Ritual. Many dinners together with local crew. So many memories. So sad from this, but I know what cancer does. Much love to the Gray family”
Gray leaves behind a wife and daughter. He was 68 years old.

articles.headline: Send in the Clown is a turn-based RPG comedy about fighting one annoying child at a birthday party where there's only one fight in the whole game
keyFacts: Send in the Clown is a turn-based RPG comedy where players control a clown named Pockets to save a birthday party.
Players must befriend party guests through minigames to recruit them for a single battle against an annoying child named Tad.
The game is approximately one hour long, features a demo on Steam, and does not use artificial intelligence.
body: I generally find it quite frustrating how limited the medium of games insists on being when it comes to engaging in a wide breadth of genres. One particular genre that its filmmaking cousin frequently utilises but is rarely seen within games is comedy. Sure, occasionally a game makes an attempt at telling a joke within a cutscene (failing more often than not (comedy's hard!)), but rarely is it a genre mechanically. So I'm quite pleased to learn of Send in the Clown, a turn-based RPG where you play as a clown that has to save a 12 year old's birthday party… and it only has one turn.

In Send in the Clown, you play as Pockets, a horrendously sad name for a clown. He has been hired to perform at Miranda's birthday party, except it's being ruined by her shitty brother Tad. Your goal, then, is to save the day by saving the party by, uh, fighting a child! That's Tad, to be clear. The problem is, Tad is a dirty trickster, and despite you being a literal adult, isn't easy to take down. Your solution to that is by trying to make friends with everyone and anyone at the party.

That involves playing a range of minigames. There's a single dad who wants to impress with his dance moves but has two left feet, so you teach him through a rhythm game. There's an exhausted mum who you help give a "much-needed break from parenting with Uncharted-style quick time events." And there's an awkward shy kid who you have to hype up a bit to get him involved. After befriending them, they essentially get added to your party (the RPG kind) and can be used to take down Tad; I'm particularly fond of the mum's incredibly powerful attack where she throws her newborn baby.

It's not just about making friends, there are a range of secrets to unlock and discover that can aid you in taking down Tad. Eventually all of this culminates in a single battle, and yes, an entire battle system was developed just for this one battle. That's commitment! It's just the bulk of the game is in the delightfully silly prep work you have to do. Best of all, it's not trying to outstay its welcome; the game is only an hour long, so it doesn't sound like any grinding will be necessary. I also greatly appreciate this note on the Steam page: "No artificial intelligence, or intelligence of any kind, was used in the making of this game."
If any of this sounds up your alley, you can try out a demo, or just shoot it a wishlist, on its Steam page.

articles.headline: The rise and fall of a MAGA princess
keyFacts: US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned on Tuesday after the White House asked for her resignation over corruption allegations.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Guilfoyle solicited funds from a donor in exchange for access to Trump officials and media figures.
Guilfoyle is a former Fox News personality and ex-fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., whom President Trump said was not family.
body: President Donald Trump and US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle in the White House on March 26, 2026. | Aaron Schwartz/Bloomberg via Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump’s ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, is out of a job after serious corruption allegations.

What happened? Guilfoyle resigned on Tuesday after being shown the door earlier in the day by Trump’s brand-new White House press secretary, who announced at a briefing that Guilfoyle had been asked to resign.

Her departure comes just six days after a bombshell Wall Street Journal story , which described Guilfoyle’s efforts to solicit money from a Trump donor, including $100,000 to pay down a credit card bill, in exchange for access to Trump officials and conservative media figures.
Guilfoyle also attempted to conceal those efforts: In one text to the donor, Eric Deters, she wrote, “What a nightmare you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing.”

Who is Guilfoyle? Fallen MAGA royalty. Guilfoyle, a former Fox News personality, is also the ex-fiancée of Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr. (and, more distantly, the ex-wife of current California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat).

There appears to be little love lost between Guilfoyle and Trump, however. On Tuesday, he told reporters that Guilfoyle “wasn’t a member of my family. She I guess dated my son a long time ago.” (The Don Jr.-Guilfoyle relationship is thought to have ended in 2024.)

Why was she forced out? Corruption allegations are not, generally speaking, dealbreakers in Trumpworld; the president and his children are all innovators when it comes to profiting off the presidency , and there’s plenty of self-dealing going on around them.

That being said, Guilfoyle may have crossed the line in two specific ways: one, her alleged corruption benefited her and not the Trump family. And two, the allegations are embarrassingly unsubtle even by the standards of the second Trump administration. The combination appears to have been too much.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: Barrios strikes after 53 seconds as Atlético pile misery on 10-man Manchester United
keyFacts: Pablo Barrios scored against Manchester United after just 53 seconds, leading to a defeat following an early goal from Ademola Lookman.
Manchester United missed several scoring opportunities through Bryan Mbeumo and Bruno Fernandes during the match.
Leny Yoro received a late red card before Lookman scored a second goal to secure the win for Atlético.
body: Michael Carrick had seen it in his players, he said, but no one else can. Not so far in the Premier League, where they have suffered their worst start in 40 years, and not here in Madrid, where Manchester United’s head coach insisted they would embrace the challenge. The reaction was coming, he promised; he had looked at them and was sure of it. Instead, they were a goal down after just 53 seconds and all that came was the old familiar sting, that early opener from Pablo Barrios and a second from Ademola Lookman condemning them to another defeat.

So much for a reaction, a rebellion: in their place a kind of resignation, a sense that maybe this is just United’s reality: a game that began badly, did not get very much better, and finished even worse. True, the result could have been different, Bryan Mbeumo unable to convert two first-half chances while Bruno Fernandes struck the bar and put an opportunity wide, but that did not diminish the feeling that something is really wrong. It may even have deepened it.
Even the late, harsh red card for Leny Yoro which can be offered in mitigation did not change a simple fact: at the end of another insipid night, United lost. United are lost, perhaps.

“Sometimes when it’s not quite going for you, you see who’s really there,” United’s manager said the night before, a message that perhaps hinted at something rotten beneath the surface, but on the opening goal no one was really there. They weren’t there on the left, where Lee Kang-in’s pass sent Álex Baena into a wide-open space; they weren’t there to close him down as he cut into the area; and they weren’t there on the right either, where Barrios was running through alone. Baena laid across and Barrios’s shot went off Ayden Heaven and into the net.

Barrios held up six fingers, the number of the club captain, Koke, whose mother had died in the hours before kick-off. From the bench Koke’s shirt was raised. All around the Metropolitano, supporters roared. This was set, it seemed.

Although another effort from Baena soon hit Lisandro Martínez, United did find a foothold and could have found a way back. Mbeumo had two clear chances in quick succession: the first, after nice footwork on the right, went wide; the second, following a neat exchange with Youri Tielemans, was stopped by Jan Oblak on the other side. From the corner, Carlos Baleba headed straight at the keeper.

That was short-lived, though, Atlético soon asserting themselves, moving the ball with a pace and conviction United couldn’t match. Barrios and Baena couldn’t be controlled, and the spaces they opened were vast. The pressure United applied tended to arrive late or not at all. On the touchline too the contrast was stark: Diego Simeone prowled, Carrick stood motionless in the corner of his technical area, chin in his hand. The Argentinian was booked for waving an imaginary card. Maybe United’s manager could try that. Something, anyway.

By half-time, Atlético had enjoyed 66% of possession. They could also have had a greater lead. Álex Grimaldo rattled a superb free‑kick off the bar and just before the break Johnny Cardoso’s sweeping finish was ruled out when the video assistant referee revealed a Marcos Llorente handball in the buildup. The second half then began with a neatly floated ball from Barrios setting up Julián Álvarez to volley against a post. Again, the space, time and the ease with which the move played out was just too big.

At the other end, Bruno Fernandes then had a wonderful opportunity to level it. Tielemans did superbly to find him, the ball sitting up and Oblak coming off his line to meet him – the kind of opportunity, in short, that is supposed to end only one way but that this time ended another.

United’s captain lifted the ball past the keeper and wide. Soon, Atlético were back again, Baena bending a shot wide, although Atlético appeared to have settled, the game drifting. That perhaps suited United: with Atlético’s threat no longer so present, the ball was theirs for the first time and the lead was still only one, opportunity there. Fernandes, increasingly involved, swung a shot against the bar.

Which was when it finally, definitively and far too easily fell apart. Suddenly, on 74 minutes, Jonathan David was running through the middle on to a Morten Hjulmand ball. Yoro went with him, grappling as they ran, and the pair fell. Although Glenn Nyberg didn’t give a foul, allowing the move to play out with David scrambling the ball to Lookman, a voice in his ear called him to the screen to watch the challenge again. When he returned, he had a red in his hand.

The decision felt harsh. It was also the end. Three minutes later, Atlético were running through United again. Grimaldo slotted a pass into David, inside the area and, although his shot was saved by Senne Lammens, Lookman was there to score. Heaven and Fernandes were removed; this was done, nothing left to fight for, not that they had fought much in the first place, the reaction postponed for some other day.

articles.headline: Will You Be Taking Time Off Work or School for GTA 6's Release Next Month?
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled to release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5, ending a 13-year wait.
Economists estimated a one billion dollar loss in productivity during launch week due to workplace absences.
Rockstar Games is promoting the release with extensive advertising, original music albums, and themed events.
body: We are just a little over 30 days away from the release of GTA 6 , which begs the question: Will you be taking time off of work or school to play it?

GTA 6 is one of the biggest pop culture events of the decade, if not in all of history, and as a result, it's expected to cause some disruption. In addition to fears that the game's highly-anticipated launch may create instability for ISPs and platform servers, many companies are also expected to have an irregular amount of employees calling out for the day. For months, fans on social media have been claiming they're putting in PTO requests well in advance of November to ensure they can have the game's release weekend available. So, will you be taking November 19 off? Let us know in the poll below, dear reader.

Economists have estimated that there will be a $1 billion loss in productivity during launch week due to people being absent from their jobs. A car tuning company known as Burger Motorsports has even announced that it will be closed on November 19 , the day of the game's release, due to an excess of employees requesting that day off. The Australian government has also released some interesting PSAs, informing citizens about their rights when it comes to taking time off around the release of GTA 6 .

The U.S. Army even offered soldiers four days of time off for the game's launch if they reenlist . NBA star Steven Adams also joked that the various sports leagues would see a drop in performance due to the release of GTA 6 . Of course, Rockstar is ensuring that, regardless of performance, sports fans are hyper-aware of its upcoming game thanks to an unprecdented GTA 6-themed NBA regular season game in Miami and a blitz of advertising at the Hard Rock Stadium where the Miami Dolphins play .

It's likely we will see a slew of other companies joining in on the GTA 6 hype as the game's launch approaches. Rockstar Games is making sure the whole world knows that its highly-anticipated release is nearly here after multiple delays. A plethora of ads have been spotted in and around Miami, New York City, and Paris. Rockstar is also investing a boatload of cash into the game's music, as it has produced an album filled with original music from the likes of Cardi B, Travis Scott, and Keith Richards . The game's radio stations will also be hosted by major musicians like Lana Del Rey, Morgan Wallen, and Bad Bunny, where they will play a variety of mainstream hits.
The 13-year wait for a new GTA game is nearly over as GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. A PC version is also rumored to release in the first quarter of 2027 .

articles.headline: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
keyFacts: Writer-director Hideo Kojima reviewed Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, stating he was impressed by its horror techniques and experience reminiscent of playing the original game.
The Resident Evil movie has earned over $320 million worldwide, becoming the highest-grossing entry in the film series to date, according to the article.
Director Zach Cregger stated he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie, but plans to direct an original film titled The Flood next.
body: Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews , said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.

"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said .

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."
Austin Abrams as Bryan in the Resident Evil movie.

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.

Another bright spot for Kojima? While he was at the theater, he picked up some physical reading materials for the divisive new Tom Cruise movie Digger. A lot of people have had a lot of things to say about that film, and we are all waiting to hear what Kojima thought of it, whenever he sees it.

The new Resident Evil has made more than $320 million worldwide , following its big debut in China where it's made $40.7 million so far . Cregger's Resident Evil movie is now the highest-grossing entry in the series to date , surpassing the previous record-holder, which was 2016's The Final Chapter ($312 million).
For more, check out GameSpot's rundown of the highest-grossing Resident Evil movies of all time .
While Cregger has said he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie , he’s done with franchise movies and is instead making an original movie, The Flood, next .

As for Kojima, he's keeping very busy with the upcoming games OD and Phsyint , both of which are in the works for Xbox. Physint will also be adapted for film and TV , while Kojima's Death Stranding is coming to the big screen as well.

articles.headline: Apple unleashes a swarm of Mac Minions to share GPU resources for large AI tasks
keyFacts: Apple researchers developed a distributed system called Minions to pool idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices for AI inference tasks.
Apple researchers stated the system reduced task queue times from over ten hours to minutes by utilizing otherwise idle hardware.
The Minions system uses four components, including a server, metadata store, executor, and watchdog, to coordinate and monitor workloads.
body: In an effort to give its employees better access to GPU resources for inference tasks, Apple has rounded up its Minions, not the animated yellow creatures, but a distributed system that puts idle GPUs across its Macs to work on AI workloads. Apple researchers describe it as "a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale machine learning inference workloads." Apple's researchers said the company has used Minions to make GPU compute more readily available to its teams. "Prior to its adoption, some inference jobs experienced queue times exceeding ten hours due to limited centralized GPU availability," the paper on Minions explains. "With Minions, tasks can often begin execution within minutes by leveraging idle macOS devices." Apple's recently released Mac mini and Mac Studio support clustering using RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) over Thunderbolt 5, allowing compute and memory to be combined to support a single AI workload. This allows, for example, loading a model too large for a single machine to accommodate. Minions is designed to create a virtual GPU cloud from connected Mac hardware to create a fault-tolerant pool of inference workers in a shared distributed inference platform. So instead of sitting idle, GPU resources can be used more readily by teams on the network. It's not necessarily intended as a way to run large models as much as it is to redistribute idle resources on the network. Minions has four primary components: Minion Server, PostgreSQL Metadata Store, Minion Executor, and Minion Watchdog. The Minion Server provides the coordination layer, receiving user requests and making them available as subtasks. The Minion Executor runs inference tasks on a Mac's GPU, uploads the results to S3, and reports execution status through the Minion Server, which maintains task metadata in PostgreSQL. And the Minion Watchdog monitors this process for failures – like one of the Macs in the network not responding – and re-assigns tasks if needed. Database stats get fed to Grafana-based dashboards for real-time visibility. Apple's approach, which focuses on hardware availability and utilization, is not the same as an Nvidia cluster, which focuses on throughput, latency, and efficient GPU utilization for large models. ®

articles.headline: Trump targets Ilhan Omar at rally following raid on her home – US politics live
keyFacts: US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Representative Ilhan Omar's home on Monday during an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the probe said it involves alleged immigration fraud, while Omar called the search political intimidation by President Trump.
President Donald Trump criticized Omar at an Ohio rally, calling her birth country of Somalia one of the worst on the planet.
body: Minnesota congresswoman Ilhan Omar said she will “not be silenced” and called a search of her Washington home part of President Donald Trump’s “intimidation” campaign.
Democratic representative Omar, an outspoken critic of the president, said she was being targeted as one of the Republican’s “political enemies”.
It comes as Trump targeted the congresswoman during a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, last night. He said Somalia, where Omar was born, is “one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet”.
He said:
She comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet. What a mess they have done - Somalia.

He urged supporters to vote Republican “if you want to stop Ohio from being plundered, ransacked and destroyed like Minnesota’s being destroyed”. In response, the crowd of Republican supporters chanted: “Deport, deport.”
US authorities conducted a predawn raid of Omar’s home in Washington, DC, on Monday as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.

A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker’s immigration paperwork filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote on social media that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” she said. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

In a statement, US House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party’s leadership in the chamber said the raid was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions” about the weaponization of the federal government against Trump’s enemies.
In other developments:

A federal judge has ordered Donald Trump’s administration to temporarily halt the broadcast of taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Effective as of 6.45pm ET on Sunday, US district judge Jennifer L Rochon of the southern district of New York issued a temporary restraining order aimed at the ads that is meant to stay in effect for at least 14 days.

The New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, compared US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)’s recent shooting of a man in the Manhattan enclave of Marble Hill to a mass shooting scene – and called for an end to the agency’s operations in his city. Mamdani’s joined MS NOW’s Jacob Soboroff for his first media interview since ICE agents shot and wounded Oscar Belgal, 28, during an enforcement operation while he was in his car with his five-year-old child also inside.

The Republican US senator Roger Marshall says he has finally paid off a bakery debt – after six years and repeated collection attempts reported by a Kansas business that had supplied a large order of treats for a 2020 election watch party. “We have absolutely no idea how this happened”, the Kansas senator wrote in a social media post containing a screenshot of the payment on a $678.75 invoice from Holly’s Sweet Treats as well as his $1,300 payment. “And we have repaid the bill … double.”

A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody. Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.

There is a manic quality to Donald Trump’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’s midterm elections to convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.

The US president offered to lower barriers against beef imports to limit surging meat prices, only to consider backtracking under pressure from the cow lobby. He offered to stop diesel exports, only to find oil companies werenot interested. He weakened fuel efficiency standards, claiming this would trim the price of a new car (and forgetting to point out it will also raise spending on gas.) In early October he started mailing $500 checks to nearly a million people touting his healthcare “wins”. Oh, and he promised adult Americans a $5,000 check if Republicans maintain control of Congress. That, too, will go nowhere.

In the face of such setbacks, maybe Trump felt he had to demonstrate he still can get something done. Most Americans think Donald Trump is profiting off the presidency in unethical or illegal ways and is focused more on his wealth than helping people like them, a new AP-NORC poll finds.

Only about two in 10 think the Republican president is doing nothing wrong, while a similar share say they don’t know enough to say.
